html:
A great mosque on the south side of the royal square of Isfahan, built from 1611 for Shah Abbas I of Safavid Iran. It is one of the masterpieces of Persian architecture.

Its gateway faces the square, Naqsh-e Jahan, but the mosque behind it turns at an angle so that its prayer hall faces Mecca. Almost every surface is covered with glazed tiles, mostly blue and yellow, and the double dome rises over 50 metres. Abbas wanted it finished fast, so builders used painted square tiles rather than slower cut tile mosaic. The work ended around 1630, just after his death.

The mosque, the square and the palaces and bazaar around it were the showpiece of the capital Abbas built to rival Istanbul, where the Süleymaniye Mosque had risen half a century earlier. After the 1979 revolution in Iran it was renamed the Imam Mosque. The square is a World Heritage Site.
sum: A great mosque on the south side of the royal square of Isfahan, built from 1611 for Shah Abbas I of Safavid Iran. It is one of the masterpieces of Persian architecture.
